key_insight: The paper adapts Regev-style quantum sampling plus lattice reduction to decompose finite Abelian black-box groups more efficiently, achieving an invariant-factor decomposition with fewer qubits and lower circuit cost.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the practical resource burden for quantum group-structure subroutines, improving scalability for algorithms that depend on hidden periodicity or algebraic decomposition.
method: Uses quantum sampling to gather O(n) group generators while keeping the lattice dimension at O(sqrt(n)).
Applies classical lattice reduction to recover integer relations and extract cyclic factors and generators.
Analyzes a common-modulus variant and compares it against Cheung-Mosca-style Sylow subgroup decomposition.
evidence_signal: From the abstract’s resource analysis, circuit gate count drops from ~O(n^2 T_op) to ~O(n^(3/2) T_op), total quantum time from ~O(n^3 T_op) to ~O(n^(5/2) T_op), and qubit use from O(n^2) to O(n).
watch_item: The improvement depends on unique encodings, reversible group operations, and lattice-reduction assumptions; real implementations may face hidden constant factors and hardware noise.
paper_title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Black-Box Abelian Group Decomposition
